text: It looks like it'll be a fun experience if you can find someone else to play co-op. Then there's 10 more like this. Burn this many wood, put coal this many times in the furnace. An order of magnitude more than you'll do naturally. Waste of time.

I'm gonna use this review as a way to express my discontent with the developers. You see, I love this game: it's easy to get into, it's hella fun, especially with friends. And as such, the multiplayer is the heart of the game. This title is the only in the series available on MacOS and it has no support for crossplay aside from Epic Store, through an iffy mod branch, btw. So they released a new game that is a rehash (All You Can Eat), price it way too high, remove Mac support and give that one crossplay capability. I'll not be buying that game, but from reviews you can see that even that game has real problems with multiplayer, FOR YEARS. Honestly, this is a pitiful way to leave their money-making franchise.
No crossplay with people who have All You Can Eat despite them being the exact same game.

Re-editing my entire review, after playing the first Overcooked almost all the way through: At first, i thought this game was a lot of fun, but i just played the first one, and now i feel like this one lacks. I mean, now we can throw stuff to make things more agile in levels, but, all the textures for almost everything have been super simplified; in the first game, for example: you could get a nice looking steak and chop it down into some hamburger meat, and it would have a nice little detailed texture. Now, in the second game, you just grab an old cartoon looking piece of meat and the hamburger is just a red circle with no details, and a brown circle when it's cooked. Same goes for a lot of other ingredients. And the difficulty of the game escalates a little too crazy here in Overcooked 2 (Dark Souls veteran speaking) In the first Overcooked, there was some challenge and difficulty, and eventually, you would need to replay some levels a few times to get all the stars required for the next levels. Here, in Overcooked 2, some levels just seem nearly impossible, with some very pushy features to make the game look challenging, but it just looks like creativity put too much in the wrong place, or a complete lack of it! The DLCs are very fun, and the Survival mode (kind of a time trial thingy) is also a ton of fun. Anyway, it is a good game after all, it corrects a lot of little glitchy things from the first title, like inputs from the pause menu being taken to the gameplay and so

EDIT: The Hangry Horde DLC, level 1-3 needing 1k points in that time limit is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ridiculous.

The save slots function is unreliable and poorly designed, you can easily lose your save with one wrong click on "new game" where you think it is "load game", and the game gives little warning about overwriting. Be careful with your saves, and I think the developers should remake their save system like other games that use world-based saves instead of slots - no one wants to go back to older saves, it is not Minecraft.

This is the worst game I've ever played in my entire life. I don't play solo, but with my girlfriend, ngl, this game is a total relationship destroyer. If you wanna break up with your partner, don't hesitate, download and play. We were stuck at a stage for freaking 3 days, which is not even the last stage of that theme. We were frustrated and couldn't find a solution to get 3 stars of that level, even though we did our best. We almost make everything perfect and haven't made any mistakes, even the tiny ones, like a slight change of the route that we used to pass the ingredients. After suffering for nearly 6 hours, we found out the problem is not with us, but that we need to be fortunate enough to meet the easier order request, which you never know when it will appear. This is apparently uncontrollable, and this will lead to the result that both of you are so disappointed and mad. Then what's next? All the emotions get exaggerated, you might burst into to argument, or get into a "cold war" situation. Now every time we play this game, we have to make sure we will still love each other after playing this game. But I have to admit, the developers really know how to manipulate people’s minds. Even though you know this game will put you in a bad mood, after a while you still get that “what if this time it works” feeling.

O jogo é tão fácil que dói. Meus dois amigos e eu conseguimos passar 95% das fases em apenas uma tentativa. Além disso, é importante destacar que, de todas as novas mecânicas de cozinha, apenas algumas conseguiram ser realmente divertidas ou capazes de render boas risadas.

​Em contrapartida, temos o Overcooked 1, no qual desempenhar um pouco mais da sua capacidade cerebral e motora é essencial para passar a maioria dos níveis e manter o 'flow' na cozinha. Isso se dá porque os mapas eram mais bem elaborados, criativos e desafiadores.
​Concluindo, na minha opinião, os devs focaram mais em quantidade do que em qualidade, e isso baixou minha nota para 6.5/10.

​E ♥♥♥♥ Kevin: todas as fases daquele cachorro maldito utilizam os mesmos utensílios, e seu balanceamento para três jogadores é horroroso. Um vai ter burnout de tanto trabalhar, enquanto os outros dois quase dormem de tão pouca coisa para fazer.

Overcooked is a game that looks really innocent and fun at a first glance, but kinda disappoints after a while

To keep things simple, the game is great at first, but the way each level derails into chaos takes away most of the fun we could be having with the gameplay.
The "cooking" mechanics are actually pretty well done, the game plays well and your character is easy to control, but the issue comes from how most levels have some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mechanic either right from the start or added halfway through that just adds stress and turns the game into an optimization simulator.
Now, I played this with my partner and we actually three starred every level first try up until chapter 4, where we played the level a second time and got the points needed then, this to say that the game isn't hard per se, the point goals are manageable, but the actual gameplay is incredibly anti-fun.
When we got into a good rhythm, things were nice, with each one of us on a different side of the kitchen, doing our things, ocasionally throwing some ingredients at eachother, having synergy, it felt really good, but that was on levels that kept the mechanics stable and had less chaos, most levels have some frustrating mechanic or something that tries to force you into a loop, like having the required ingredients on a different platform that is constantly moving out of reach or keeping us apart 60% of the time, which makes things much harder. Difficulty - The first go around was very easy, even for 2 first time players to the series. We beat every level on the first or second try, not a brag, it just wasn't that hard and we didn't have to make that many adjustments to get the high score each time. I was happy to see there's essentially a new game + once you beat every level. Instead of putting all the skills you've learned to the test you just make a ton of food and throw it on the floor then start the clock. This was the deciding factor for me to give a thumbs down, I get that you may want to make the first go through easy for some gamers but the second go around should challenge you to better yourself at the game mechanics and order of operations you use in order to complete dishes. After playing the first level again in new game + with my friend numerous times and really optimizing each process we still were not even close to the par score. We watched a video of how 2 others beat the level and after seeing them just make food and throw it on the ground before starting the clock I realized that the whole experience is empty. I wanted a fun local co-op game that I could play with my 9-year old son. On paper this looks ideal. However, in practice the game is way too difficult from the start and it quickly becomes impossible to play. We finally gave up playing entirely because we couldn't proceed in the main storyline. I can't believe the developers didn't think about this. I suppose there is a setting somewhere for unlimited time or something, but this is beyond the point. A game meant to be fun to play should gradually become more difficult and the pacing in this game is definitely wrong.

Game in itself is pretty fun. But all the little things that the developers ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up make it infuriating. Multiplayer works worse that Remote Play Together, so if you want to play co-op, I would recommend buying only a single copy and playing through that. Native Linux version has no controller support, while the Windows version running through Proton ♥♥♥♥♥ up the controller input by randomly releasing or double pressing buttons. Steam cloud saves are not synced between platforms and even better for some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason the saves are encrypted ([b]IT'S A FCKING CO-OP GAME[/b]), at least for Steam users it's their SteamID so not really an issue. But developers had to find a way to also ♥♥♥♥ it up, so if you hava a GOG offline install of the game, the saves are encrypted with your [b]HWID[/b]. Overall, the game could be a million times better if not for the developer's incompetence.

What the actual ♥♥♥♥ is this digital dumpster fire called "Overcooked 2" online mode?! I'd rather have my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stitched shut with barbed wire than suffer through another second of this lag-infested, brain-dead multiplayer catastrophe.

Trying to play co-op is like herding meth-fueled squirrels through a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hurricane. The netcode is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥ I swear it runs on two tin cans and a wet string. My "teammate" in Tokyo might as well be cooking from the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ International Space Station—by the time my "chop" command registers, the whole kitchen is already engulfed in digital flames.

And these randoms online? Their IQ combined couldn't fill a teaspoon. I've seen tree stumps with better reflexes than these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Some bastard spent three whole minutes just waving at a tomato like it was his estranged father, while I'm getting gangbanged by five erupting soup pots. The "disconnected" pop-up appears more often than actual ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ recipes—this game's servers must be powered by a hamster having a seizure.

Whoever designed this multiplayer diarrhea should be forced to play it using Nintendo Switch Joy-Cons with drifting sticks while being waterboarded with spoiled mayonnaise. This isn't a game—it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ psychological warfare experiment disguised in cartoon aesthetics. 0/10, my controller now has a hole in it and my soul has filed for divorce.
